questions.prompt: What money is used in Sri Lanka?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Sri Lanka is the Sri Lankan rupee.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Sri Lanka about 65,610 square kilometres; Taiwan about 36,197 square kilometres; East Timor about 14,919 square kilometres; Palau about 466 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Sri Lanka?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Ethnic make-up” part of the Sri Lanka article.

questions.proof: Their language is Sinhala which is an Indo-Aryan language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Sri Lanka shares a sea boundary with the _____ in the south-west and India in the north-west.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sri Lanka article.

questions.proof: Sri Lanka shares a sea boundary with the Maldives in the south-west and India in the north-west.

questions.prompt: Which continent is Sri Lanka in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Sri Lanka on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Sri Lanka on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
